dark_pattern: Partner-billed plans cannot be canceled on Spotify's site — you must cancel through the billing partner shown under Payment.
steps: Go to Manage your plan on your Spotify account page.
Select Cancel subscription.
Your Premium stays until your next billing date, then your account switches to Spotify Free.
If you do not see the option to cancel, check the Payment section of your account page — your plan may be billed through a partner company.
Note: on a $0.00 free trial, your plan switches to Spotify Free immediately upon canceling.

dark_pattern: Subscriptions billed through a third party must be canceled with that provider, not on Peacock.
steps: Log in to your Peacock account.
Select Cancel All Subscriptions.
Follow the on-screen prompts until a confirmation appears; Peacock also sends a confirmation email.
Your plan remains active through the end of your current subscription term.
If you do not see the cancel option, your subscription may be billed by a third party — cancel it through that provider.
Peacock states it does not provide refunds or credits unless legally required.

dark_pattern: Apple- and Google Play-billed memberships cannot be canceled on YouTube — cancel through the billing platform.
steps: Tap your profile picture, then Paid memberships.
Select the Premium (or Music Premium) membership.
Select Continue to cancel.
Choose a cancellation reason, then select Next.
Select Yes, cancel.
You keep your benefits until the end of the billing period.
Memberships billed through Apple or Google Play must be canceled through Apple or Google Play.
Sign in to your Microsoft account and find your subscription, then select Manage.
On the next page, select Cancel and follow the prompts.
If you see Turn on recurring billing instead of a Manage link, the subscription is already set to expire - nothing further to do.
retention_warning: Microsoft will offer plan switches or pauses first. Billed through Apple or a third party? Cancel there instead.
